title: One-loop renormalisation of the Standard Model with a non-anticommuting γ₅
subtitle: The renormalised Lagrangian operator by operator: one fermion family, BMHV scheme with sterile partners, MS-bar, finite Slavnov–Taylor-restoring counterterms, Feynman gauge, unbroken and broken phase.
status:
This page presents the complete one-loop renormalised action Sren=S0+δS(1)+ΔSST(1) of the Standard Model with one fermion family, regularised in d=4−2⁢ϵ dimensions with the BMHV treatment of γ5: for every operator its coefficient in the classical action, in the singular counterterm and in the finite restoring counterterm, its Feynman rules, the one-loop graphs that determine it and the theory behind it. It is a picture of what first-class Lagrangian support in HepKIT and a multi-loop BMHV automation are meant to produce directly; today it is assembled from the sources listed below.

Generated by the automation. The Python package hepkit_renorm of this repository starts from the model specification of the one-family Standard Model (gauge group, chiral multiplets, scalar doublet, classical four-dimensional Lagrangian, linear gauge fixing at ξ=1) and derives everything else: the sterile partners, ghosts and BRST sources, the regularised action and the breaking Δ1, the classes of Green's functions, the operator bases, the one-loop graphs (enumerated by the package and cross-checked against the HepKIT diagram generator) and their pole and evanescent finite parts, the singular counterterm, the finite breaking X1 and the restoring counterterm under the report's normalisation conditions. On this run the twenty renormalisation constants, the eight beta functions, the 71 non-zero components of X1 and all 97 restoring coefficients (39 of them non-zero) agree with the report, and all fifteen checks of the run pass. The graphs drawn on this site are the graphs of that run, rendered with HepKIT at the level of multiplets.

Taken from the report. The theory texts, the names of the basis monomials, the section and page references and the cross-checks quoted in the texts are taken from the report One-loop renormalisation of the Standard Model with a non-anticommuting γ₅. The package has no broken-phase representation; the operators of the broken phase are derived on this site from those of the unbroken phase by the shift of the Higgs doublet and the rotation to the mass basis of the report, and are checked against the automation's order store and against the report's broken-phase formulas.

Not covered. Two-loop quantities (the construction beyond one loop is argued in the report and tested on a toy graph only); the dependence on the gauge parameter (all results hold in the Feynman gauge); the Rξ gauge and the complex-mass scheme, which the report describes but does not compute; broken-phase loop functions other than the zero-momentum check of the massless gauge bosons, in particular the finite tadpole and the two-point functions at non-zero momentum; several fermion families and flavour mixing.

types.tree: Classical action S0, including gauge fixing, ghosts and the BRST source terms.
types.pole: Singular counterterm δS(1) on a non-evanescent operator, continued to d dimensions as in Section 3.8.6. Its coefficient includes 116π21ϵ.
types.evanescent: Singular counterterm on an evanescent operator, one that vanishes in four dimensions. Its coefficient includes 116π21ϵ.
types.finite: Finite symmetry-restoring counterterm ΔSST(1)=116π2⁢∑αrα⁢Qα, which restores the Slavnov–Taylor identity.
types.breaking: Insertion Δ1=𝐬S0 of the tree-level breaking. It is not part of the action; it is listed for its Feynman rule.

conventions:
• Dimensional regularisation with d=4−2⁢ϵ (the lunate ϵ); the Levi-Civita symbol is the curly εμνρσ.
  • Barred objects are four-dimensional, hatted objects −4+d-dimensional.
  • A vertex function V is listed for each operator; the Feynman rule is i times V. All momenta are incoming unless a leg label says otherwise.
  • Renormalisation constants such as δZH include the factor 116π21ϵ; the finite counterterm is ΔSST(1)=116π2⁢∑αrα⁢Qα.
  • Feynman gauge ξ=1, one fermion family, MS-bar. The broken-phase Lagrangian follows from the shift H→Hv+φ.
